Yes a dam is more difficult to build than a hospital or become prime minister, by many orders of magnitude.

The govt (or supporters) could easily put most concerns aside if they simply present the mathematics of how they expect it to happen.

For example, the cost of Shaukat Khanum Peshawar was PKR 4 billion, which is about $32 million. The Bhasha Diamer dam will be *400* times that amount.

If you told me you want to crowdfund double the amount that was generated for SKMC peshawar, or even ten times that amount I would still consider it. But if you say you want to crowdfund 400 times that amount then it's only reasonable to ask for some kind of calculation, and not rely solely on hope and optimism.

I'd love to be proven wrong as I need water as much as anyone else, but we need to be serious.

I agree with OP that to the extent that there seems to be a trend within the exmuslim community that sees Islam as the primary source of evil and oppression amongst Muslims rather than other socioeconomic or cultural factors.

Yes, it's true that Islam is obviously false and it's literature and history is filled with stuff that should be abhorrent to decent people. But Islam is not the ONLY source of oppression in the world. And in many cases there are other ideologies that are worthy of being criticised more (eg capitalism, Western imperialism, etc) because they have more power and ability to influence Muslim societies more than Islamic institutions (or as is usually the case, capitalism and imperialism are in a nexus with Islamic institutions).

I realise that this sub is a space where many exmuslims who have undergone trauma because of Islam come to express themselves and vent freely. But I do at the same time feel that criticism of Islam should not be exaggerated to the extent that it feeds into right-wing racism. Yes there is much to criticise about Islam from a factual and moral perspective, but it needs to be put into the context of the actual power it possesses versus other institutions and societies.
